steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Conceptually, a transformer is a stack of identical processing blocks that repeatedly answer one question about every token in a sequence:  
“Which other tokens should I look at, and how should I combine what I find?”  

Here is the idea, step by step:

1. Turn symbols into vectors  
   • Each input token (word, sub-word, character, etc.) is mapped to a dense embedding vector.  
   • Because order matters, a positional encoding is added so the model can distinguish “dog bites man” from “man bites dog”.

2. Let every token pay “attention” to every other token  
   • For each token, the model forms three short vectors:  
     – Query: What am I looking for?  
     – Key: How do other tokens advertise what they contain?  
     – Value: What information do they actually carry?  
   • Similarity(Query, Key) gives a score saying how relevant another token is.  
   • After soft-maxing those scores, the token builds a weighted average of all Values.  
   • This operation is called self-attention (or cross-attention if queries come from one sequence and keys/values from another).

3. Look through several “heads” at once  
   • Instead of one Query-Key-Value projection, we make many in parallel (multi-head attention).  
   • Each head learns to focus on different patterns: syntax, long-distance agreement, topic words, etc.  
   • Heads are concatenated and linearly mixed back into the main stream.

4. Mix and refine locally  
   • After the attention step, a small feed-forward neural network (the same for every position) further processes each token’s vector.  
   • Both attention and feed-forward sublayers are wrapped in residual (skip) connections plus layer normalization, making optimization easier and enabling very deep stacks.

5. Stack the blocks  
   • An encoder is several of these blocks stacked; it transforms an input sequence into contextualized vectors.  
   • A decoder is another stack that, at each layer, attends both to its own earlier outputs (masked self-attention) and to the encoder’s output (cross-attention).  
   • GPT-style models keep only the decoder portion and use masking to generate text autoregressively.

6. Train end-to-end with simple objectives  
   • For translation: predict the next target token given previous targets and the encoded source sentence.  
   • For language modeling: predict the next token in a sequence.  
   • Gradients flow through attention, feed-forward, and embeddings, updating everything jointly.

Key intuitions  
• Attention lets the model dynamically choose what context matters instead of relying on fixed-width windows or recurrence.  
• Sharing the same weights across positions plus massive parallelism (no recurrence) makes transformers efficient on modern hardware.  
• Depth (many layers) and width (many heads) give them the capacity to model complex relationships in language, vision, protein sequences, and beyond.
